FINDING_ID: ROUND7_F001  
SEVERITY: 0.89  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION: 0.84  
VERIFIED: FALSE  
DESCRIPTION: **`DynamicManager.process_round()` does not validate that each `Finding.round_idx` matches the manager’s actual `round_idx`, and `update_fingerprints()`/convergence logic ignore the embedded round on the finding entirely.** This is distinct from prior findings about trusting caller-supplied round numbers in general: here the deeper issue is that contradictory per-finding chronology is silently accepted into *three* downstream systems at once. A mixed batch containing stale findings from an earlier round and fresh findings from the current round will be clustered together, used for novelty/convergence, and used to update live fingerprints as if they all belonged to the same round. That breaks the temporal semantics of `D_decay`, `kappa_set`, and marginal yield simultaneously. PROPOSED_FIX: reject any finding whose `round_idx != self.fsm.current_round`, or normalise by overwriting round indices at ingestion after validating provenance.

FINDING_ID: ROUND7_F002  
SEVERITY: 0.86  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION: 0.81  
VERIFIED: FALSE  
DESCRIPTION: **`DynamicManager.process_round()` accepts `Finding.model_id`s that have no corresponding successful response in `responses`, and those orphan findings still affect convergence and fingerprint updates.** Prior findings noted acceptance of unknown/inactive models broadly, but the missed cross-cutting issue is response–finding referential integrity: a model can contribute findings to the system state without ever having produced a parseable, non-empty, non-timeout response in that round. Because findings are passed separately from responses, a caller can accidentally or adversarially attach high-severity findings to a failed or absent model and still drive `kappa`, `stop`, and adaptive fingerprints. PROPOSED_FIX: enforce that every finding is attributable to a known, active model with a matching non-failed response for the same round, or explicitly separate “externally injected findings” from model-originated findings in the API and metrics.

FINDING_ID: ROUND7_F003  
SEVERITY: 0.84  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION: 0.77  
VERIFIED: FALSE  
DESCRIPTION: **`update_fingerprints()` can raise `KeyError` if `failure_handler.active_models` contains a model ID not present in `_live_fingerprints`/`_round_metrics`.** This is a deeper consequence of the unknown-model contamination path: `FailureHandler.detect_failure()` and `get_recovery()` use `setdefault()` and can create history for arbitrary `model_id`s, but `DynamicManager` only initialises `_live_fingerprints` and `_round_metrics` from the original pool. If such an unexpected ID ever becomes or remains “active” in `FailureHandler`, `update_fingerprints()` blindly does `old_fp = self._live_fingerprints[model_id]` and `self._round_metrics[model_id].append(obs)`, crashing mid-round. PROPOSED_FIX: make `FailureHandler` reject unknown models entirely, and defensively validate that `active_models ⊆ _live_fingerprints.keys()` before fingerprint updates.

FINDING_ID: ROUND7_F004  
SEVERITY: 0.82  
FLAW_CLASS: 4  
ABSTRACTION: 0.79  
VERIFIED: FALSE  
DESCRIPTION: **The manager emits no event for the chosen recovery action, even though recovery decisions materially mutate system state.** Prior findings covered missing recovery execution and some event taxonomy gaps, but the missed part is observability of *decision* itself: `get_recovery()` chooses `RETRY`, `RETRY_EXTENDED`, `RETRY_CLARIFIED`, `DEGRADE`, `DOWNGRADE_ROLE`, `EXCLUDE`, or `ABORT`, yet no corresponding `ManagerEvent` is emitted at decision time except indirect failure-type events. Downstream supervisors therefore cannot distinguish “timeout detected” from “timeout detected and excluded” without re-deriving policy from internal history. PROPOSED_FIX: emit an explicit recovery-action event after every `get_recovery()` call, with action, triggering failure type, repetition count, and whether active set changed.

FINDING_ID: ROUND7_F005  
SEVERITY: 0.80  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION: 0.76  
VERIFIED: FALSE  
DESCRIPTION: **`DynamicManager.process_round()` never records non-response failures for active models absent from `responses`, so omission is not just tolerated—it is invisible to failure history and role penalty history.** Some prior findings noted that missing responses are treated as success-by-omission. The deeper missed consequence is state skew across subsystems: omitted active models receive no `FailureHandler` record, no `RoleAssignment.record_failure(False/True)` entry, no recovery decision, and no event, so per-model histories become length-misaligned and biased toward whichever models happened to appear in the `responses` dict. This directly distorts failure-history penalties used in reassignment. PROPOSED_FIX: derive the expected responder set from allocation/live active models, synthesize timeout-or-missing failures for absent responders, and record an explicit success/failure bit for every expected active model each round.

FINDING_ID: ROUND7_F006  
SEVERITY: 0.77  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION: 0.71  
VERIFIED: FALSE  
DESCRIPTION: **`RoleAssignment.record_failure()` is called only for models present in `responses`, so `_failure_history` lengths diverge across models and `phi_hist` ceases to represent a per-round failure rate.** This is related to missing-response handling but is a distinct statistical defect: `phi_hist = sum(hist)/len(hist)` assumes histories cover comparable round sets. In practice, a model omitted from some rounds accumulates a shorter denominator, making its apparent failure rate artificially high or low depending on which rounds were recorded. Since reassignment multiplies capability by `(1 - phi_hist)`, role changes are driven by inconsistent sample windows rather than actual failure frequency. PROPOSED_FIX: append a status for every active model each round (`failed`, `succeeded`, or `not_scheduled`) and compute penalties over aligned round indices or a fixed recent window.

FINDING_ID: ROUND7_F007  
SEVERITY: 0.74  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION: 0.72  
VERIFIED: FALSE  
DESCRIPTION: **`ConvergenceDetector.add_round_findings()` accepts negative `duration` values, which invert the sign of `kappa_rate()` and can artificially increase convergence after a busy round.** Existing findings discussed noisy or semantically wrong rate baselines, but not invalid time domains. Because `_rate(r)` uses `len(classes) / max(dt, 1e-10)`, any negative duration is silently coerced to `1e-10`, producing an astronomically large rate for that round; the combined metric then clamps only the lower bound via `max(0, kappa_rate)`, effectively turning corrupted timing data into a hard zero on one round and potentially unstable diagnostics elsewhere. PROPOSED_FIX: validate `duration > 0` at ingestion and reject or explicitly mark invalid rounds instead of regularising bad data into extreme rates.

FINDING_ID: ROUND7_F008  
SEVERITY: 0.72  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION: 0.69  
VERIFIED: FALSE  
DESCRIPTION: **`DiminishingReturnsDetector.add_round()` accepts arbitrary `yield_value` and `mean_abstraction_new` without bounds or monotonicity checks, allowing internally impossible cognitive-yield trajectories to be stored as if valid.** Prior findings covered negative/zero round economics, but not the unchecked yield domain itself. Since `yield_value` is supposed to be cumulative `Y^(<=r)`, it should normally be non-negative and non-decreasing under the module’s own semantics. A caller can pass a decreasing or NaN yield, after which `marginal_value()`, smoothing, and `remaining_value_estimate()` operate on nonsensical state without any guard. PROPOSED_FIX: validate finite non-negative inputs and, for externally supplied cumulative yields, enforce `yield_value >= previous_yield` unless the API explicitly supports retractions/corrections with a separate flag.

FINDING_ID: ROUND7_F009  
SEVERITY: 0.70  
FLAW_CLASS: 4  
ABSTRACTION: 0.73  
VERIFIED: FALSE  
DESCRIPTION: **The event stream uses `model_id="system"` as a sentinel in `ManagerEvent`, but `model_id` is otherwise a real model identifier and there is no reserved-value contract.** This can collide with an actual model named `"system"` and make event attribution ambiguous in `events_by_model()`. The bug is cross-cutting because the same field is used for both entity-scoped failure events and global orchestration events. PROPOSED_FIX: split event scope into explicit fields such as `subject_type`/`subject_id`, or reserve and validate sentinel identifiers so they cannot overlap with real model IDs.

FINDING_ID: ROUND7_F010  
SEVERITY: 0.68  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION: 0.66  
VERIFIED: FALSE  
DESCRIPTION: **`DynamicManager.__init__()` does not fail fast on duplicate `finding_id` or `task_id` domains because those identifiers are never centrally validated, yet later APIs imply uniqueness semantics.** Prior findings covered duplicate `task_id` and duplicate `model_id`; the missed extension is identifier hygiene across the full artifact. `Finding.finding_id` is presented as an identifier but is never checked for uniqueness even within a round, making audit trails and external dedup impossible. Combined with unstable equivalence classes and mutable stored references, post-hoc reasoning about “which finding was counted” becomes unreliable. PROPOSED_FIX: validate uniqueness for task IDs, model IDs, and per-round finding IDs at ingestion boundaries, or document clearly that these are opaque labels with no uniqueness guarantee and stop using “id” terminology.

FINDING_ID: ROUND7_F011  
SEVERITY: 0.66  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION: 0.64  
VERIFIED: FALSE  
DESCRIPTION: **`FailureHandler.should_abort()` can return `False` even when there is no PM role in `role_map`, because it only aborts if it finds a PM and that PM is inactive.** If external mutation or earlier corruption removes the PM entry entirely, `pm_id` stays `None` and the method falls back to `len(_active_models) < k_min`. With default `k_min=1`, a system with active workers but no PM can continue despite the class docstring treating PM continuity as a hard requirement. This is stronger than prior findings about PM invariants relying on shared dicts: the abort gate itself fails open when the invariant is broken. PROPOSED_FIX: assert exactly one PM exists in `role_map` before processing rounds and make absence of a PM an unconditional abort/error.

FINDING_ID: ROUND7_F012  
SEVERITY: 0.63  
FLAW_CLASS: 6  
ABSTRACTION: 0.61  
VERIFIED: FALSE  
DESCRIPTION: **`process_round()` takes a `tasks` argument only to satisfy signature symmetry, but because it is ignored while `round_cost` is caller-supplied, the manager cannot cross-check the economics of the round against the work it claims to have processed.** Prior findings noted that `tasks` are unused and allocation is not persisted. The deeper missed consequence is that the diminishing-returns subsystem becomes completely decoupled from actual dispatched work: a caller may report arbitrary `round_cost` unrelated to the given tasks, and the manager has no internal consistency check available because it discarded allocation and ignores tasks here. PROPOSED_FIX: require the actual `Allocation` used for the round, recompute or sanity-check cost from allocation/tasks/models, and reject economically inconsistent round reports.

These are the new findings I can justify from the artifact without repeating already-listed issues.
